Have those four bring the necessary equipment and come down from the mountain overnight. I have work for them.” Dai Zong departed.

p.src: Presently a soldier came in from outside the camp to report that Hu Cheng of the Hu Family Manor in the western village had brought cattle and wine and was requesting an audience. Song Jiang ordered that he be admitted. Hu Cheng came before the central command tent, bowed twice, and pleaded, “My younger sister acted rashly in her youthful ignorance and unwittingly offended your dignity. She has now been captured, and I beg the general to pardon her. The unfortunate fact is that she was already betrothed to the Zhu Family Manor, and the other day, in an ill-advised burst of valor, she landed herself in bonds. If the general will graciously release her, whatever goods you require shall be respectfully presented at your command.” Song Jiang said, “Please sit down, and we shall talk. Those scoundrels of the Zhu Family Manor behaved most outrageously and wantonly bullied our stronghold. That is why we have marched against them to avenge the wrong; we bear no grievance against your Hu family. It was only because your sister led men to seize our Wang Ying, the Stumpy Tiger, that we returned the courtesy and captured her. Return Wang Ying to me, and I shall return your sister to you.” Hu Cheng replied, “Unfortunately, that worthy fellow has already been taken away by the Zhu Family Manor.” Scholar Wu asked at once, “Where is our Wang Ying now?” Hu Cheng said, “He is now chained and imprisoned in the Zhu Family Manor. How would a humble man like me dare go and demand him back?” Song Jiang said, “If you do not retrieve Wang Ying and return him to me, how can you expect to take your sister home?” Scholar Wu said, “Brother, do not speak so. Just heed one proposal of mine: from now on, whenever any disturbance arises at the Zhu Family Manor, day or night, your manor must send no one to their aid. And should anyone from the Zhu Family Manor flee to you, bind him there and then. If we succeed in capturing their people, we shall then escort your sister back to your honored manor. At present, however, she is not in this camp. Several days ago, we had her sent to the mountain stronghold, where she is being cared for at Lord Song’s residence. Set your mind at ease and go home. We have our own plan here.” Hu Cheng said, “This time I shall most certainly not dare go to their aid. If anyone from their manor should indeed seek refuge with me, I shall bind him and present him beneath the general’s standard.” Song Jiang said, “If you do that, it will be worth more to me than a gift of gold and silk.” Hu Cheng bowed his thanks and departed.

p.src: Meanwhile, Sun Li changed the inscription on his banners to read “Sun Li, Commandant of the Dengzhou Forces,” and led his entire company to the rear gate of the Zhu Family Manor. Those watching from atop the manor walls saw the Dengzhou banners and sent word inside. When Luan Tingyu heard that Commandant Sun of Dengzhou had come to visit, he told the three Zhu brothers, “Commandant Sun is my sworn brother. We studied martial arts under the same master from childhood. I wonder what brings him here today?” Taking more than twenty horsemen with him, he opened the manor gate, lowered the drawbridge, and went out to welcome them. Sun Li and his companions all dismounted, and the two parties exchanged the customary courtesies. Luan Tingyu asked, “Brother, you were stationed on guard in Dengzhou. What brings you here?” Sun Li replied, “The commander-in-chief’s headquarters issued an order transferring me here to guard the city of Yunzhou and defend it against the brigands of Liangshan Marsh. As my route brought me this way, and I heard that you were here at the Zhu Family Manor, I came especially to visit you. I had meant to come by the front gate, but I saw that large numbers of troops were encamped both at the village entrance and before the manor, and I did not wish to blunder into them. So I deliberately searched through the village, asking my way along the minor paths until I reached the rear of the manor, that I might come in and pay my respects to you.” Luan Tingyu said, “For several days now we have been fighting the brigands of Liangshan Marsh without respite. We have already captured several of their chieftains and imprisoned them here in the manor. We need only seize their bandit chief Song Jiang, and then we shall deliver the lot to the authorities. By heaven’s blessing, you have now come to take command in this region. It is like adding flowers to brocade, or rain falling on drought-stricken shoots.” Sun Li laughed. “Though I possess little ability, just watch me help you capture a few of those scoundrels and bring your achievement to completion.” Luan Tingyu was delighted. He then led the whole company into the manor, after which the drawbridge was raised again and the gate shut. Sun Li and his company settled their carts, baggage, men, and horses, changed their clothes, and assembled in the front hall. They met Squire Zhu and his three sons, Zhu Long, Zhu Hu, and Zhu Biao; the entire household came to receive them before the hall. Luan Tingyu led Sun Li and the others into the hall. When the courtesies were concluded, he said to Squire Zhu, “This worthy brother of mine is Sun Li, nicknamed the Sick Yuchi. He holds the post of commandant of the Dengzhou forces. He has now been transferred here by order of the commander-in-chief’s headquarters to take charge of Yunzhou’s defenses.” Squire Zhu said, “This old man, too, resides within your jurisdiction.” Sun Li replied, “My humble office is hardly worth mentioning! In the days to come, I shall have to look to you, Squire, for guidance and support.” The three Zhu brothers invited their honored guests to be seated. Sun Li inquired, “You must have been greatly wearied in body and spirit by these many days of battle.” Zhu Long replied, “As yet, neither side has won or lost. And all you honored brothers have endured no small hardship on the road.” Sun Li then had Aunt Gu escort Madam Yue and the wives of the two Xie brothers to the rear hall to pay their respects to the women of the household. He called Sun Xin, Xie Zhen, and Xie Bao forward, presented them, and said, “These three are my brothers.” Pointing to Yue He, he said, “This gentleman is a clerk sent here from Yunzhou on official business.” Pointing to Zou Yuan and Zou Run, he said, “These two are military officers sent from Dengzhou.” Though Squire Zhu and his three sons were shrewd men, they saw that Sun Li had brought womenfolk and children, a great quantity of baggage, carts, and horses, and that he was Master Luan Tingyu’s sworn brother. They therefore harbored no suspicions at all, but busied themselves slaughtering cattle and horses, laying out a banquet for the company, and drinking and feasting with them.

p.src: A day or two passed. On the third day, a manor soldier reported, “Song Jiang has redeployed his forces and is attacking the manor again.” Zhu Biao said, “I shall mount up and capture this bandit myself.” He went out through the manor gate, lowered the drawbridge, and charged forth at the head of more than a hundred cavalrymen. Before long he met a column of some five hundred troops. At their head rode a chieftain with bow bent and arrows at his side, spurring his horse and brandishing his spear: it was Hua Rong, the Little Li Guang. At the sight of him, Zhu Biao urged his horse forward with spear leveled, while Hua Rong likewise galloped out to fight him. Before Lone Dragon Ridge, the two fought for more than ten bouts without either gaining the upper hand. Hua Rong feigned an opening, wheeled his horse, and fled, luring Zhu Biao into pursuit. Just as Zhu Biao was about to spur after him, someone behind who knew Hua Rong called out, “General, do not pursue him! Beware of hidden missiles. That man is exceedingly skilled with the bow.” Hearing this, Zhu Biao reined his horse around and abandoned the pursuit. He led his troops back into the manor and raised the drawbridge. When they looked toward Hua Rong, they saw that he too had withdrawn with his troops. Zhu Biao rode all the way to the front hall before dismounting, then went into the rear hall to drink wine. Sun Li asked, “Which bandit did the young general capture today?” Zhu Biao replied, “Among those scoundrels is a fellow called Hua Rong, the ‘Little Li Guang.’ His spear technique is truly formidable. We fought for more than fifty bouts, and then the scoundrel fled. I was just about to pursue him, but the soldiers said he was skilled with the bow, so each side withdrew its troops and returned.” Sun Li said, “Tomorrow, though my abilities are slight, just watch me capture several of them.” At the banquet that day, Yue He was called upon to sing, and everyone was delighted.

p.src: When the evening banquet ended, they stayed another night. At noon on the fourth day, a manor soldier suddenly reported, “Song Jiang’s forces have come before the manor again.” In the hall, the three sons, Zhu Long, Zhu Hu, and Zhu Biao, donned their armor and went outside the manor’s front gate. Gazing into the distance, they heard gongs sounding, drums thundering, men shouting, and banners waving; the enemy had already drawn up its battle lines opposite them. Zhu Chaofeng sat atop the manor gate, with Luan Tingyu on his left and Commandant Sun on his right; the three heroes of the Zhu family and the many companions Sun Li had brought were arrayed on either side. Presently they saw Lin Chong, the “Panther Head,” loudly hurling abuse from Song Jiang’s lines. Zhu Long lost his temper, ordered the drawbridge lowered, snatched up his spear, and mounted. Leading one or two hundred horsemen, he gave a great shout and charged straight at Lin Chong’s formation. Drums thundered beneath the manor gate, while archers and crossbowmen on both sides held the battle lines in check. Lin Chong leveled his eighteen-foot Serpent Spear and fought Zhu Long. They battled for more than thirty bouts without either gaining the advantage. Both sides sounded their gongs, and the warriors reined back their horses. Zhu Hu flew into a rage, mounted with sword in hand, galloped before the lines, and loudly challenged Song Jiang to single combat. Before he had finished speaking, a warrior rode out from Song Jiang’s formation: it was Mu Hong, the “Unrestrained,” coming to fight Zhu Hu. The two fought for more than thirty bouts, again without a victor. Seeing this, Zhu Biao grew furious. He snatched up his spear, sprang onto his horse, and led more than two hundred riders toward the battle line. From Song Jiang’s ranks, Yang Xiong, the “Sickly Guansuo,” charged out on horseback with a spear to fight Zhu Biao. When Sun Li saw the two forces locked in combat before the lines, he could restrain himself no longer. He told Sun Xin to fetch his whip and spear, had his armor, helmet, and battle robe brought and put them on, then ordered his own mount led over. The horse was called the Black Stallion. Once it was saddled and its three belly straps fastened, he hung the Tiger-Eye Steel Whip from his wrist, grasped his spear, and mounted. At the sound of a gong from Zhu Family Manor, Sun Li rode out before the lines. In Song Jiang’s formation, Lin Chong, Mu Hong, and Yang Xiong all reined in their horses and stood before the ranks. Sun Li spurred forward and said, “Watch me capture these rogues.” Sun Li wheeled his horse around and shouted, “If there is anyone in your bandit ranks who knows how to fight, let him come out and face me!” As bridle bells rang within Song Jiang’s formation, a horse came galloping out. When the men looked, they saw it was Shi Xiu, the “Desperate Third Son,” coming to fight Sun Li. The two horses met, and both spears rose together. After they had fought fifty bouts, Sun Li feigned an opening and let Shi Xiu thrust his spear in. Dodging aside, he lightly plucked Shi Xiu from his horse, carried him beneath his arm straight to the manor, and flung him down, shouting, “Tie him up!” The three Zhu brothers threw Song Jiang’s troops into confusion and drove them all off. The three brothers recalled their forces and returned beneath the gate tower. When they saw Sun Li, everyone saluted him with clasped hands in admiration. Sun Li then asked, “How many bandits have been captured altogether?” Zhu Chaofeng replied, “First we caught Shi Qian; afterward we seized a spy, Yang Lin, and also captured Huang Xin. At Hu Family Manor, the “Ten-Foot Blue” captured Wang the Short Tiger; on the battlefield we took Qin Ming and Deng Fei; and now, General, you have captured this Shi Xiu—the very rogue who burned down my inn. That makes seven in all.” Sun Li said, “Do not harm a single one of them. Quickly prepare seven prison carts and put them inside. Give them food and wine and tend to their health; do not let hunger weaken them and spoil the spectacle. When we capture Song Jiang, we shall escort them all together to the Eastern Capital, so that the whole realm may spread the fame of the three heroes of Zhu Family Manor.” Zhu Chaofeng thanked him, saying, “It is our great fortune to have your aid, Commandant. Surely Liangshan Marsh is doomed to destruction.

p.src: On the fifth day, Sun Li and his companions were strolling idly about the manor. At about eight in the morning, after breakfast, a manor soldier came to report, “Today Song Jiang has divided his troops into four columns and is coming to attack our manor.” Sun Li said, “What would it matter if he divided them into ten columns? Tell your men not to panic. They need only make their preparations early. First prepare grappling hooks and lassos. We must capture them alive; taking them dead does not count.” Everyone in the manor donned armor. Zhu Chaofeng personally led a company up to the gate tower to look. Due east he saw a body of troops led by Lin Chong, the “Panther Head,” with Li Jun and Ruan Xiao’er behind him, altogether more than five hundred men and horses. Due west were another five hundred or so troops, led by Hua Rong, the “Lesser Li Guang,” with Zhang Heng and Zhang Shun following behind. Looking from the southern gate tower, they saw another five hundred or so troops led by three chieftains: Mu Hong, the “Unrestrained”; Yang Xiong, the “Sickly Guansuo”; and Li Kui, the “Black Whirlwind.” Troops surrounded the manor on every side; war drums thundered in unison, and mighty battle cries arose. Hearing this, Luan Tingyu said, “These rogues mean to fight in earnest today. We must not underestimate them. I shall lead a body of troops out the rear gate and attack the force to the northwest.” Zhu Long said, “I shall go out the front gate and attack the force to the east.” Zhu Hu said, “I too shall go out the rear gate and attack the force to the southwest.” Zhu Biao said, “I shall go out the front gate myself and capture Song Jiang, the most important of the bandit chiefs.” Zhu Chaofeng was delighted and rewarded them all with wine. Each man mounted and led more than three hundred riders galloping out of the manor gates, while all the rest guarded the compound and raised battle cries before the gate towers. By then Zou Yuan and Zou Run had concealed their great axes and were waiting at the left side of the prison gate. Xie Zhen and Xie Bao had hidden their concealed weapons and stayed close to the rear gate. Sun Xin and Yue He had already taken up positions on either side of the front gate. Mistress Gu first assigned soldiers to protect Lady Yue, then took up her twin sabers and prowled before the hall, waiting only for the signal to strike.

I shall lead a body of troops out the rear gate and attack the force to the northwest.”
Zhu Long said, “I shall go out the front gate and attack the force to the east.”
Zhu Hu said, “I too shall go out the rear gate and attack the force to the southwest.”
Zhu Biao said, “I shall go out the front gate myself and capture Song Jiang, the most important of the bandit chiefs.”
Zhu Chaofeng was delighted and rewarded them all with wine.
Each man mounted and led more than three hundred riders galloping out of the manor gates, while all the rest guarded the compound and raised battle cries before the gate towers.
By then Zou Yuan and Zou Run had concealed their great axes and were waiting at the left side of the prison gate.
Xie Zhen and Xie Bao had hidden their concealed weapons and stayed close to the rear gate.
Sun Xin and Yue He had already taken up positions on either side of the front gate.
Mistress Gu first assigned soldiers to protect Lady Yue, then took up her twin sabers and prowled before the hall, waiting only for the signal to strike.

p.src: Now at Zhu Family Manor, the war drums sounded three times and a cannon fired. The front and rear gates were thrown open, the drawbridges lowered, and all the troops charged out together. The soldiers poured out through four approaches and scattered in every direction to join battle. Sun Li came last with a dozen or so soldiers and took his stand upon the drawbridge. Inside the gate, Sun Xin raised the banner they had brought upon the gate tower, while Yue He brandished his spear and came straight out singing their signal song. When Zou Yuan and Zou Run heard Yue He singing, they gave several whistles, swung their great axes, and promptly cut down dozens of the manor guards watching the prison gate. They opened the prison carts and released the seven tigers; each seized a weapon, and together they raised a battle cry. Aunt Gu drew her two swords, rushed straight into the rooms, and killed every woman she found, one with each stroke. Seeing that matters had turned against him, Squire Zhu was about to throw himself into a well when Shi Xiu struck him down with one slash and cut off his head. Those dozen or so heroes split up to attack the manor troops. At the rear gate, Xie Zhen and Xie Bao set fire to the stacks of horse fodder, and black flames surged into the sky.

p.src: When the four divisions saw fire rising from the manor, they joined forces and pressed forward. Seeing the flames within the manor, Zhu Hu was the first to race back. Sun Li, guarding the drawbridge, shouted, “Where do you think you’re going, you wretch?” He blocked the way across the bridge. Zhu Hu realized what was happening, wheeled his horse around, and charged back toward Song Jiang’s formation. There Lü Fang and Guo Sheng thrust with both halberds at once, toppling Zhu Hu and his horse to the ground. The soldiers swarmed over him and hacked him into pulp. The vanguard scattered and fled. Sun Li and Sun Xin welcomed Song Gongming into the manor. Meanwhile, on the eastern front, Zhu Long could no longer withstand Lin Chong and galloped toward the rear of the manor. When he reached the drawbridge, he saw Xie Zhen and Xie Bao at the rear gate hurling the manor servants’ corpses one by one into the flames. Zhu Long hastily turned his horse and fled north. Suddenly he ran into the Black Whirlwind, who sprang forward, swung his twin axes, and promptly chopped down the horse’s legs. Caught unprepared, Zhu Long pitched headlong from the saddle, and Li Kui split his head open against the ground with a single blow of his axe. When fleeing manor soldiers brought Zhu Biao the news, he dared not return but made straight for Hu Family Manor. Hu Cheng ordered his retainers to seize and bind him, and they were escorting him to Song Jiang. They happened to meet Li Kui, who struck off Zhu Biao’s head with a single axe blow, sending all the manor retainers fleeing in every direction. Li Kui raised his twin axes again and came hacking at Hu Cheng. Seeing how badly matters stood, Hu Cheng mounted his horse and fled into the wilderness. Abandoning his home to save his life, he escaped to Yan’an Prefecture. Later, during the restoration, he also became a military officer and general.

He ordered the lesser bandits to lead away all the horses and loaded every kind of treasure in the manor onto forty or fifty pack animals. Then he set the manor compound ablaze and returned to present his spoils.

p.src: By then Song Jiang had seated himself in the main hall of Zhu Family Manor. The chieftains came one after another to report their achievements: four or five hundred prisoners had been taken, more than five hundred fine horses seized, and cattle and sheep captured beyond counting. Song Jiang was delighted, but said, “It is only a pity that the valiant Luan Tingyu was killed.” While he was still lamenting, someone reported, “The Black Whirlwind has burned Hu Family Manor and is bringing heads to present.” Song Jiang said, “Hu Cheng came and surrendered to us the other day. Who ordered him to kill this man? And why did he burn down his manor?” Then the Black Whirlwind appeared, his whole body smeared with blood and two broad axes thrust into his belt. He strode up to Song Jiang, made a deep salute, and said, “Your brother killed Zhu Long, and your brother cut down Zhu Biao too. That scoundrel Hu Cheng escaped, but I wiped out Squire Hu’s entire family. Your brother has come especially to claim his merit.” Song Jiang barked, “There are witnesses who saw you kill Zhu Long, but how can you claim that you killed the others?” The Black Whirlwind said, “The killing was going well, so I chased on toward Hu Family Manor. There I ran straight into the elder brother of Ten Feet of Steel, escorting Zhu Biao out. I killed Zhu Biao with one blow of my axe; it’s only a pity that scoundrel Hu Cheng got away. As for his manor, I killed every last soul there.” Song Jiang shouted, “You wretch! Who told you to go there? You knew that Hu Cheng brought cattle and wine the other day and came to surrender. Why did you ignore my words, go off on your own to kill his entire family, and deliberately disobey my command?” Li Kui said, “You may have forgotten, but I haven’t. The other day that scoundrel set that damned woman on you, chasing you down to kill you, and now you want to do him a favor. You never even married his sister, yet already you’re thinking of him as your brother-in-law and their father as your father-in-law.” Song Jiang shouted, “Tie Niu, stop talking nonsense! How could I possibly take that woman as my wife? I have my own plans for her. You black brute, how many did you take alive?” Li Kui answered, “Who the hell has patience for that? Anyone I saw alive, I cut down.” Song Jiang said, “You disobeyed my military command and by rights should be beheaded. For now, your merit in killing Zhu Long and Zhu Biao shall offset the offense. If you disobey orders again, you will certainly not be spared.” The Black Whirlwind laughed. “Even if I’ve lost the merit, at least I had a fine time killing them.”

p.src: Then the strategist Scholar Wu arrived at the manor leading a column of troops, and they all offered Song Jiang wine to congratulate him. Song Jiang consulted with Wu Yong and proposed sweeping away the entire village around Zhu Family Manor. Shi Xiu reported, “Old Zhongli is a benevolent and virtuous man. He guided us and rendered us a great and loyal service. There are other good-hearted, decent villagers here as well; we must not unjustly destroy such good people.” After hearing this, Song Jiang told Shi Xiu to find the old man and bring him there. Before long Shi Xiu returned with old Zhongli and brought him into the manor to pay his respects to Song Jiang and Scholar Wu. Song Jiang took a bundle of gold and silk and rewarded the old man, saying for all the villagers to hear, “Were it not for the favor we owe this old man, I would have swept away your entire village and spared not a single household. Because your household has practiced goodness, I shall therefore spare all the people throughout this district.” Old Zhongli could only bow repeatedly. Song Jiang continued, “For many days we have disturbed you common folk here. Today we have broken Zhu Family Manor and rid your village of this scourge. Every household shall be granted one shi of grain, as a token of our goodwill.” He appointed old Zhongli to supervise its distribution, while all the surplus grain in Zhu Family Manor was loaded onto carts. The gold, silver, and other valuables were distributed as rewards among the generals and the three armies. The remaining cattle, sheep, mules, horses, and other livestock were taken back to the mountain for use there. By breaking Zhu Family Manor, they obtained five hundred thousand shi of grain. Song Jiang was overjoyed. The chieftains, great and small, assembled the troops and horses and prepared to depart. They had also gained a number of new chieftains: Sun Li, Sun Xin, Xie Zhen, Xie Bao, Zou Yuan, Zou Run, Yue He, and Aunt Gu, together with the seven heroes they had rescued. Sun Li and the others brought along their own horses and possessions, as well as their families and Madam Yue, and followed the main army up the mountain. The villagers along the way came out with their elders and children, bearing fragrant flowers, lanterns, and candles, and bowed in gratitude beside the road. Song Jiang and all his commanders mounted together. They divided the troops into three columns and set out; in the vanguard, whips tapped against golden stirrups, while the rear guard sang songs of victory in unison. Indeed:

p.src: Outlaws may be called outlaws, yet they are no common outlaws; The strong may be called strong, and truly strong they are. Only to destroy evil and root out villainy do they turn, for a time, to raiding homes and seizing goods. The countryside hates the oppression of local tyrants; the villages rejoice in the aid bestowed by righteous men. The assembled tigers, moved by fellowship, rescued the chicken thief and dog snatcher; The Lone Dragon, left unaided, could not detain the Flying Tiger or the Sky-Striking Eagle. They duly supplied provisions worth many thousands, enough to fill the marsh; And sacrificed countless people and livestock besides, enough to trample Liangshan flat.

p.src: The tale now divides in two. Let us speak of Li Ying, the Sky-Striking Eagle. His arrow wound had only just healed, and he remained behind closed gates at his manor, never venturing out. In secret he regularly sent men to learn what was happening at the Zhu Family Manor; when he heard that Song Jiang had destroyed it, he was half alarmed and half delighted. Presently a manor servant came in to report that the prefect had arrived with thirty or fifty men and was asking about the affair at the Zhu Family Manor. Li Ying hurriedly ordered Du Xing to open the manor gates and lower the drawbridge, then welcomed them inside. With his injured arm supported by a strip of white silk, Li Ying came out to receive them and invited them into the manor's front hall. The prefect dismounted, entered the hall, and took the central seat. To one side sat the judicial clerk; below him were a head constable and several attendants, while the foot of the steps was crowded with warders and jailers. After Li Ying had bowed, he stood before the hall. The prefect asked, “What do you know of the slaughter at the Zhu Family Manor?” Li Ying replied, “After Zhu Biao shot me with an arrow and wounded my left arm, I kept my gates shut and dared not go outside. I know nothing of what truly happened.” The prefect said, “Nonsense! The Zhu Family Manor has lodged a written accusation saying that you conspired with the powerful bandits of Liangshan Marsh and brought in their troops to destroy the manor. Only the other day you also accepted saddled horses, sheep, wine, colored silks, gold, and silver from them. How can you deny it?” Li Ying pleaded, “I am a man who knows the law. How would I dare accept anything from them?” The prefect said, “Your word is hard to believe. We shall take you to the prefectural seat, where you may confront your accusers and settle the matter.” He shouted for the jailers to seize Li Ying and take him to the prefectural seat to answer the Zhu family's charges. The head constables and attendants on either side bound Li Ying, and the whole company crowded around the prefect as he mounted his horse. The prefect then asked, “Which man is Steward Du, Du Xing?” Du Xing replied, “I am he.” The prefect said, “Your name is also in the accusation. Take him along. Put him in chains as well.” The whole company went out through the manor gates. Thus they seized Li Ying and Du Xing, left the Li Family Manor, and marched their prisoners onward without pause. They had traveled scarcely more than thirty li when Song Jiang, Lin Chong, Hua Rong, Yang Xiong, Shi Xiu, and a body of troops burst out beside a wood and blocked their path. Lin Chong thundered, “The heroes of Liangshan Marsh are all assembled here!” The prefect and his men dared not resist. Abandoning Li Ying and Du Xing, they fled for their lives. Song Jiang shouted for his men to pursue them. They chased them for some distance, then returned and reported, “If we had caught them, we would have killed that damned prefect too, but we could not tell which way he went.” They untied Li Ying and Du Xing, opened their locks, and brought over two horses for them to ride. Song Jiang said, “Would you be willing, honored sir, to hide at Liangshan Marsh for a while?” Li Ying said, “That cannot be. You killed the prefect; it has nothing to do with me.” Song Jiang laughed. “How would the authorities ever consent to make such a distinction for you? Once we leave, they will certainly implicate you. Since you are unwilling to join the outlaw band, rest at our stronghold for a few days. When we have learned that the danger has passed, it will not be too late for you to come down from the mountain.” At that moment Li Ying and Du Xing had no choice but to go. Surrounded by that great host, how could they possibly turn back? The entire force wound its way back to Liangshan Marsh. Chao Gai and the other chieftains in the stronghold beat drums and played flutes as they came down the mountain to welcome them. After serving wine to wash away the dust of the journey, everyone went up to the Hall of Righteous Assembly in the main stronghold and sat in a circle like the spread of a fan. Li Ying was invited forward and introduced to all the chieftains. When the formal greetings were over, Li Ying addressed Song Jiang: “The two of us have now escorted you, General, back to the main stronghold and have met all the chieftains. We do not mind remaining here to serve you, but I do not know what has become of the old and young in my household.

p.src: Please allow me to go down the mountain.” Scholar Wu laughed. “You are mistaken, honored sir! Your honored family has already been brought to the stronghold. Your manor has been burned to bare earth. Where could you return to?” Li Ying did not believe him, but soon he saw carts, servants, and horses coming up the mountain in group after group. When Li Ying looked closely, he saw that they were his own manor servants and all the old and young of his household. Li Ying hurried over to question them. His wife said, “After the prefect arrested you, two patrol inspectors arrived with four constables and about three hundred local troops to confiscate our property. They courteously ordered us into the carts, then took away every chest and trunk in the house, along with the cattle, sheep, horses, donkeys, mules, and everything else. Then they set fire to the manor and burned it all down.” When Li Ying heard this, he could only lament his misery. Chao Gai and Song Jiang both stepped down from the hall and bowed in apology. “We brothers have long heard of your great worth, honored sir. That is why we resorted to this stratagem. We earnestly beg your forgiveness.” Faced with these words, Li Ying had no choice but to yield. Song Jiang said, “Please let your family rest in the side rooms behind the hall for now.” Li Ying also saw that many chieftains there had their wives, children, and elderly relatives living about the front and rear halls. He therefore said to his wife, “We have no choice but to accept their arrangement.” Song Jiang and the others then invited him to the front of the hall, where they chatted at leisure, and everyone rejoiced. Song Jiang teased him, saying, “Honored sir, watch while I summon the two patrol inspectors and that prefect to meet you.” The man disguised as the prefect was Xiao Rang; the two disguised as patrol inspectors were Dai Zong and Yang Lin; the judicial clerk was Pei Xuan; and the attendants were Jin Dajian and Hou Jian. Then he called the four constables forward: they proved to be Li Jun, Zhang Shun, Ma Lin, and Bai Sheng. When Li Ying had looked at them all, he stood wide-eyed and open-mouthed, unable to speak. Song Jiang shouted for the junior officers to slaughter cattle and horses at once, so they might feast the honored gentleman and celebrate the twelve chieftains newly come to the mountain: Li Ying, Sun Li, Sun Xin, Xie Zhen, Xie Bao, Zou Yuan, Zou Run, Du Xing, Yue He, and Shi Qian; The two women chieftains, Hu Sanniang and Gu Dasao. They, together with Lady Yue and Li Ying's family, were given a separate banquet in the rear hall. All the troops, from high to low, received rewards of their own. Music and drums resounded through the main hall, and the many heroes drank until evening before dispersing. Each of the newly arrived chieftains was assigned quarters and settled in.

They courteously ordered us into the carts, then took away every chest and trunk in the house, along with the cattle, sheep, horses, donkeys, mules, and everything else.
Then they set fire to the manor and burned it all down.”
When Li Ying heard this, he could only lament his misery.

Chao Gai and Song Jiang both stepped down from the hall and bowed in apology. “We brothers have long heard of your great worth, honored sir. That is why we resorted to this stratagem. We earnestly beg your forgiveness.”
Faced with these words, Li Ying had no choice but to yield.
Song Jiang said, “Please let your family rest in the side rooms behind the hall for now.”

Li Ying also saw that many chieftains there had their wives, children, and elderly relatives living about the front and rear halls. He therefore said to his wife, “We have no choice but to accept their arrangement.”
Song Jiang and the others then invited him to the front of the hall, where they chatted at leisure, and everyone rejoiced.
Song Jiang teased him, saying, “Honored sir, watch while I summon the two patrol inspectors and that prefect to meet you.”
The man disguised as the prefect was Xiao Rang; the two disguised as patrol inspectors were Dai Zong and Yang Lin; the judicial clerk was Pei Xuan; and the attendants were Jin Dajian and Hou Jian.
Then he called the four constables forward: they proved to be Li Jun, Zhang Shun, Ma Lin, and Bai Sheng.
When Li Ying had looked at them all, he stood wide-eyed and open-mouthed, unable to speak.

Song Jiang shouted for the junior officers to slaughter cattle and horses at once, so they might feast the honored gentleman and celebrate the twelve chieftains newly come to the mountain: Li Ying, Sun Li, Sun Xin, Xie Zhen, Xie Bao, Zou Yuan, Zou Run, Du Xing, Yue He, and Shi Qian;
The two women chieftains, Hu Sanniang and Gu Dasao. They, together with Lady Yue and Li Ying's family, were given a separate banquet in the rear hall.
All the troops, from high to low, received rewards of their own.
Music and drums resounded through the main hall, and the many heroes drank until evening before dispersing.
Each of the newly arrived chieftains was assigned quarters and settled in.

p.src: The next day, another banquet was prepared, and all the chieftains were invited to witness and approve the arrangement. Song Jiang summoned Wang the Stunted Tiger and said, “When we were at Mount Qingfeng, I promised to arrange a marriage for you. It has weighed upon my mind ever since, for I have yet to fulfill that promise. Today my father has a daughter, and he shall take you as his son-in-law.” Song Jiang then went himself to invite Squire Song forth and led Hu Sanniang, the “Ten-Foot Serpent,” to the banquet.
